item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has begun using drones to airlift wounded soldiers from the front line, a first operational use of this method. Russian drones have struck Yandex data centres, disrupting Russian court hearings, and have also hit a Kyiv hospital, injuring five people. NATO has increased its Black Sea deployment as Russian attacks intensify, while Poland is seeking an explanation from Ukraine over a drone incident that occurred in Lithuania. The conflict has caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police have detained ten settlers suspected of attacking a US photographer, a French mayor and other civilians in the West West Bank, torching cars and olive trees and wounding farmers. The United Nations reports that 340 children have been killed in Gaza despite a ceasefire, according to UNICEF. Israeli fire has killed four people in Gaza, as medics confirm. The Israeli military says a senior Hamas security officer was killed in an airstrike. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran has intensified its maritime campaign, attacking container ships and a tug in the Strait of Hormuz and launching missiles near the UAE, while its IRGC conducts drone and artillery strikes in Iraqi Kurdistan after appointing a new defence minister. Lavrov visited Tehran and publicly backed Iran, raising questions about Moscow’s role. Houthi forces have repeatedly struck Yemeni army and government training camps, killing dozens of recruits in Shabwa and elsewhere. Pakistan has suspended border trade with Iran following cross-border violence. 123 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces have stepped up strikes, killing 53 soldiers in a training camp and raising the death toll from a later strike on a government camp to 73, the highest single loss since the war resumed. A missile hit a residential area in Taiz, killing two teenage girls, and the Houthis attacked a besieged city that the UN says is at grave risk. Saudi Arabia is preparing defensive measures, including deploying fighter jets to protect its territory against further Houthi attacks. The conflict produced 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
The Sudanese army is conducting drone strikes on civilian sites, including a market in Abyei where more than 150 people were killed, a mourners' gathering and a fuel market where over 300 were killed, and a market in southern Sudan with hundreds of casualties. The Rapid Support Forces are also using drones to hit economic targets such as gold-mining areas in West Kordofan and near the Egypt border, causing dozens of civilian deaths. These attacks extend drone use from combatant targets to markets, mourners and economic sites, expanding civilian exposure to aerial strikes. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopian forces have installed a caretaker administration in Tigray and are advancing toward the Eritrean border, while a pro-government militia says it has seized the regional airport and reports Eritrean forces suffered losses there. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the fighting. Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced elections will be held within six months and that Western Tigray will be settled through constitutional processes. A drone strike in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 73 people, and the TPLF claims to have killed 1,511 Ethiopian soldiers in recent fighting. The conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Islamic State-linked militants attacked civilians in Mali's Menaka region, killing dozens of people. Mali's military and allied armed groups continue to commit abuses against civilians. The violence is concentrated in the Sahel, especially Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso, where the multi-sided conflict has persisted since 2012. The latest reports describe a large civilian massacre by jihadist fighters, adding to ongoing attacks on non-combatants. The conflict caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen in Plateau killed NSCDC officer Distu Garba Audu and abducted a businessman, while separate attacks on herders in the same state left two dead and six injured. In Kaduna, bandits abducted five people, including a one-month-old baby, and a fisherman reported his fingers were cut off. Police freed a Catholic priest and seven other abductees in Benue, and bandits killed three policemen on duty in Zamfara. Islamist jihadists burned an evangelist alive in Adamawa, kidnapped a Catholic priest in Benue and struck bases. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan: the situation
item.description:
Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani security forces along the Kurram border, killing a Pakistani officer and several militants in Balochistan, while Pakistan suspended trade at two Iran border crossings amid violence and smuggling concerns. A dispute over the Zangali checkpost is disrupting operations at the Torkham crossing, adding to a broader toll on trade with both Iran and Afghanistan. Pakistan is seeking broader security partnerships, moving to ratify a defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey that expands cooperation beyond bilateral frameworks. The UCDP recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt: the situation
item.description:
Armed men shot a Kuki civilian in Kangpokpi and villagers were killed in Khongbal Tangkhul, prompting protests in Manipur where effigies of the chief minister and deputy chief minister were burned and bodies of killed civilians were placed outside the chief minister’s residence, leading to calls for resignations. Police arrested multiple suspects in Manipur, seizing firearms and explosives after attacks in Nongshum, Khongban Sanurok, and a recent ambush in Kangpokpi, and detained three individuals during a combing operation in Kangpokpi. In Kashmir, the Northern Army commander reviewed security and operational preparedness while buses bound for the region were attacked in Punjab and Haryana, with passengers labeled terrorists. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Philippines: the situation
item.description:
Chinese naval and coast guard vessels intensified monitoring of a U.S. warship near a disputed shoal while also entering waters near the Pratas Islands and Scarborough Shoal, prompting the Philippines to summon China’s ambassador over threatening remarks and to demand an apology. Vice Admiral Rommel Supangan took command of the Philippine Coast Guard and led a rescue of four people, including a child, on Hagonoy Island, Surigao del Sur. Taiwan’s coast guard and maritime forces repelled sixteen mainland Chinese ships in a coordinated operation near the Pratas Islands. The United States and the Philippines conducted their sixteenth bilateral maritime exercise in the West Philippine Sea, and there were 176 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Mexico's cartel violence: the situation
item.description:
Mexican authorities arrested five suspects linked to the murders of Canadian mining workers and detained a man known as El Talibán and four others in a kidnapping case, while protesters demanding clean water in Guadalajara were wounded as they tried to enter Jalisco's Government Palace. Ukrainian-origin fiber-optic drones are being trained for use by Mexican cartels, prompting continued border patrol challenges from drone incursions. A judge sentenced three men to 159 years each for the murder of three surfers on a remote beach, and an Arizona child murder suspect was detained in Mexico after a decade on the run. 37 battle-related deaths in 1996, according to UCDP.

The Syrian court continues trials of three defendants in transitional justice cases, and regional partners discussed recovery and food security at Doha and FAO meetings. item.title: Southern Thailand: the situation
item.description:

A Chinese suspect was detained in Bangkok after attempting a 100,000 baht border crossing, and Malaysia appointed a new facilitator for southern Thailand peace talks. Cambodia and Thailand agreed on confidence-building measures at a UNCLOS meeting and discussed easing maritime border tensions, while the WTO and multilateral partners reviewed progress on a supply-chain finance initiative. European and Ecuadorian police cooperation produced 20 arrests in a major drug-trafficking bust, and nightly curfews were imposed across Ecuador from November 1 to 10 under a state of emergency. The Shingal mayoral post, vacant for nine years, is now open for nominations, and Jordan's king reaffirmed support for regional sovereignty and security. item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Fitgharan forces now hold the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, expanding fighting in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and the ICRC treated 148 wounded after heavy combat in Baidoa. Ethiopia announced the withdrawal of more than 3,000 troops from Somalia as its own civil war intensifies, and Ethiopia has refused to intervene in the South West State conflict. Somaliland and Puntland were designated as "friendly" in an Israeli security framework, and Somalia is screening travelers after Kenya confirmed an imported Ebola case and has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets. Kenyan-led forces and Erik Prince's contractors are striking gang positions in Port-au-Prince and Kenscoff with drones and air support, while Sri Lankan police, army and a Bangladesh UN advance team have been deployed to Haiti. The United Nations renewed sanctions on Haiti and allocated US$75 million for life-saving aid to 507,000 people. Four soldiers are missing after a gang attack and five Salvadoran soldiers disappeared following an ambush, indicating ongoing threats to foreign troops. Elections remain on hold as gangs adapt to the security crackdown, and 193 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
